Excellent work, everyone. This is exactly why we hold this roundtable before filing. Let me summarize the complete set of changes that must be incorporated before I will sign this renewal submission:

First, the compliance certification cannot be signed as currently drafted — Marisol's PFAS finding at MW-4 at 2.4 micrograms per liter, well above the 0.7 action level, means the certification must be revised to account for that reportable exceedance.

Second, the monitoring plan must be updated to identify exactly 8 monitoring wells for quarterly sampling.

Third, the operating limits section must be revised from 25,000 to 18,000 gallons per month for solvent throughput, based on Grant's confirmation from plant engineering.

Fourth, the renewal package must include a corrective-action plan addressing the MW-4 exceedance, and we need a first progress report submitted 45 days after filing, per the new agency guidance Daniel identified.

Fifth, the stakeholder section must include a completed tribal consultation record with the nearby tribal nation before the agency will consider the file complete — Nia, that engagement needs to be initiated immediately given the September 30 timeline.

Marisol, I agree with your point about coordinating the corrective-action plan with the revised solvent throughput limit — those two items must be consistent with each other in the final package.

I will not sign this submission until all five items are resolved and incorporated. I'd like each of you to come back with a timeline for completing your respective items so we can confirm we'll be ready before September 30. Are there any other outstanding issues anyone has not yet raised?
